gap_description: Barter, unregistered work, informal credit, undeclared trade and other activity are weakly observed.
why_it_matters: Formal economic statistics can miss substantial local activity.
attack_strategy: Compare household surveys, tax gaps, labour-force surveys, transaction studies and source-specific estimates.
falsification_question: Would the apparent economic structure remain if plausible informal activity were included?
alternative_explanations: Measurement under-reporting; definitional differences; illegal activity hidden by design.

gap_description: Actual local venues, independent media, festivals, clubs and amateur groups are not equivalent to consumption measures.
why_it_matters: Consumption can remain high while local production capacity erodes.
attack_strategy: Build place-time inventories of active organisations, facilities, participants, outputs and survival.
falsification_question: Does high consumption persist after local production capacity falls?
alternative_explanations: Migration; digitisation; consolidation; changes in reporting.

gap_description: Places may be discussed extensively while producing little local journalism or agenda-setting information.
why_it_matters: External attention is not the same as local voice.
attack_strategy: Separate about/by/for/with-place information and compare local versus external contribution and attention.
falsification_question: Does high external attention predict local information capacity, or can the two diverge?
alternative_explanations: Tourism; crisis coverage; platform effects; population size.

gap_description: Formal education counts do not capture practical skills, maintenance capacity, organisation or institutional memory.
why_it_matters: Capability stocks can erode before outputs visibly decline.
attack_strategy: Measure practitioners, transmission, retirement/exit, maintenance and institutional-memory indicators.
falsification_question: Can observed capability decline be distinguished from changing demand or technology substitution?
alternative_explanations: Automation; migration; ageing; changing task requirements.

gap_description: Local extraction, imports, processing, waste, recycling and exports are poorly represented compared with national aggregates.
why_it_matters: A place's physical metabolism can differ sharply from national averages.
attack_strategy: Track directed material flows with quantity, processing stage, destination and recovery status.
falsification_question: Does the apparent prosperity of a place persist when physical inputs, waste and exports are included?
alternative_explanations: Boundary choice; supply-chain relocation; accounting conventions.

gap_description: Security provision can be distributed among state, private, community, militia, religious, customary and criminal providers.
why_it_matters: Recorded crime alone cannot describe who actually provides security or coercive capacity.
attack_strategy: Map provider presence, functions, coverage, reliance and relationships to other providers.
falsification_question: Do changes in recorded crime remain after changes in security-provider structure are accounted for?
alternative_explanations: Reporting changes; enforcement intensity; conflict; institutional substitution.

gap_description: Annual indicators can miss rapid transitions and regime shifts.
why_it_matters: Boom, decline, reconstruction and consolidation can occur between annual observations.
attack_strategy: Use event/change-point metadata and non-annual observations where defensible.
falsification_question: Would the inferred transition timing change materially with monthly/quarterly data?
alternative_explanations: Seasonality; reporting delays; boundary changes; temporary shocks.

gap_description: Variable definitions, boundaries and denominators change over time and across sources.
why_it_matters: Apparent trends may be measurement artefacts.
attack_strategy: Require definition, methodology, denominator, boundary and source-vintage metadata.
falsification_question: Does the relationship survive a defensible harmonisation or source-stratified analysis?
alternative_explanations: Real change; reclassification; survey redesign; boundary revisions.

gap_description: Proposed patterns can become stories if alternative explanations and falsification tests are not required.
why_it_matters: Epistemic guardrails are necessary for autonomous discovery.
attack_strategy: Require alternative explanations, confounders, reverse causality, selection bias, measurement change and falsification tests.
falsification_question: What observation would make the obvious interpretation wrong?
alternative_explanations: Confirmation bias; collider bias; omitted variables; model selection.

gap_description: Cross-border cultural influence needs exposure, consumption, adoption, local reproduction, hybridisation and return-flow measures.
why_it_matters: A single cultural-share number hides direction and mutation.
attack_strategy: Track directed place-time flows and variant parentage.
falsification_question: Does an apparent foreign-origin influence disappear when local reproduction and hybridisation are separated?
alternative_explanations: Common global platforms; language; migration; ownership; production location.

gap_description: Employed people / vacancies / advertised jobs / filled jobs are not equivalent and are rarely measured consistently.
why_it_matters: Using one as a proxy for another obscures labour market structure.
attack_strategy: Collect all four measures with consistent definitions and denominators for comparable places.
falsification_question: Would labour market analysis change materially if all four distinctions were properly recorded?
alternative_explanations: Confirmation bias; poor survey design; administrative data limitations.

gap_description: Housing stock / occupied housing / available housing are not equivalent and are rarely measured consistently.
why_it_matters: Using one as a proxy for another obscures housing conditions.
attack_strategy: Collect all three measures with consistent definitions and denominators for comparable places.
falsification_question: Would housing analysis change materially if all three distinctions were properly recorded?
alternative_explanations: Administrative data limitations; definition variability; boundary changes.

gap_description: Crime occurring / reported / recorded / arrests / prosecutions / convictions are not equivalent and are rarely measured consistently.
why_it_matters: Using one as a proxy for another obscures criminal justice dynamics.
attack_strategy: Collect all six measures with consistent definitions and boundaries for comparable places.
falsification_question: Would criminal justice analysis change materially if all six distinctions were properly recorded?
alternative_explanations: Reporting changes; reclassification; enforcement intensity; legal process differences.

gap_description: Incidence / prevalence / diagnosis / mortality are not equivalent and are rarely measured consistently.
why_it_matters: Using one as a proxy for another obscures health dynamics.
attack_strategy: Collect all four measures with consistent definitions and denominators for comparable places.
falsification_question: Would health analysis change materially if all four distinctions were properly recorded?
alternative_explanations: Diagnosis coding changes; definition drift; demographic shifts.

gap_description: Cultural exposure / consumption / adoption / production / influence are not equivalent and are rarely measured consistently.
why_it_matters: Using one as a proxy for another obscures cultural dynamics.
attack_strategy: Collect all five measures with consistent definitions for comparable places and periods.
falsification_question: Would cultural analysis change materially if all five distinctions were properly recorded?
alternative_explanations: Platform metrics; consumption data; ownership records do not capture adoption or influence.

gap_description: Word-level language evolution with reliable dates and geographic provenance is not systematically tracked.
why_it_matters: Borrowing direction, semantic change and geographic spread lack reliable provenance.
attack_strategy: Build a word-level language evolution register with etymology, borrowing direction, geographic spread and semantic change timestamps.
falsification_question: Would language change analysis be improved with word-level provenance?
alternative_explanations: Common global platforms; language leveling; migration patterns.

gap_description: Informal workers and their characteristics are not captured in formal labour statistics.
why_it_matters: The informal workforce can be substantial yet invisible to policy and planning.
attack_strategy: Survey informal employment; cross-reference with tax informal sector estimates; collect occupation and sector data.
falsification_question: Does the informal workforce share change when formal employment shifts?
alternative_explanations: Economic cycles; digitisation; regulatory changes.

gap_description: Attention and information production are not equivalent to physical presence or importance.
why_it_matters: High attention does not guarantee local influence or importance.
attack_strategy: Separate explicit, inferred and unknown connection to a place; measure information production separately from attention.
falsification_question: Does high external attention predict local information capacity, or can the two diverge?
alternative_explanations: Tourism; crisis coverage; platform effects; population size.

gap_description: Comparable small-area socioeconomic data across every country/territory is not available.
why_it_matters: Aggregating to national level loses local variation; local data uses incompatible definitions.
attack_strategy: Produce harmonised small-area estimates with documented definitions, boundaries and methods for every country.
falsification_question: Would cross-country analysis be improved with truly comparable small-area data?
alternative_explanations: Boundary revisions; survey redesign; administrative data differences.

gap_description: Long historical series with stable geographic boundaries is not available.
why_it_matters: Annual data with changing boundaries prevents observing true long-term trends.
attack_strategy: Reconstruct historical series using consistent boundary definitions and documented methodology changes.
falsification_question: Would trend analysis be improved with long series and stable boundaries?
alternative_explanations: Boundary revisions; survey redesign; administrative data differences.

gap_description: Cross-domain relationships are not consistently preserved as first-class, time-bounded edges between entities.
why_it_matters: Analyses can otherwise reconstruct relationships ad hoc and lose direction, reciprocity, persistence, network structure or relationship-level provenance.
attack_strategy: Use the general interaction graph to record entity-to-entity relationships, temporal validity, evidence status, strength where available, observations and event links.
falsification_question: Do important cross-domain findings change when network structure is represented explicitly rather than inferred from co-occurring observations?
alternative_explanations: Entity-resolution errors; missing links; reporting bias; false relationship inference.
